title: Never shake a crying baby, and step away if you are overwhelmed
summary: Both the US CDC and UNICEF say never to shake a baby, and both say that if crying overwhelms you, put the baby in a safe place and step away briefly.
body: The CDC 2-month page says never to shake a baby, because shaking can damage the brain or cause death. If the caregiver is getting upset while the baby is crying, CDC says to put the baby in a safe place, walk away, and check every 5 to 10 minutes. It adds that infant crying is often worse in the first few months and then gets better. UNICEF Parenting says that no matter how upset a caregiver feels, never shake, hit, or shout at the baby, and that if you are upset, put the baby in a safe place and take a short break of 5 to 10 minutes before trying again. Neither page prints an emergency telephone number in those sentences. This is what those two pages say. It is not a treatment protocol, and it is not advice written for one household.

sources.note: US government public domain. Supports the do-not-shake tip, the safe-place step, the 5-to-10-minute check, and the sentence that crying is often worse in the first months.
